title: Browser doesn't show iframe contents anymore
line: The Web Browser widget now shows iframes and other remote content in local HTML files.
explanation: Qt WebEngine's default settings block pages loaded from file:// URLs from loading remote URLs, and the widget never changed that, so any iframe pointing at a website showed Chromium's error page. The Plasma 5 (QtWebKit) widget allowed it. The change sets localContentCanAccessRemoteUrls on the widget's WebEngineView.

commits.message:
applets/webbrowser: let local pages show remote content

Qt WebEngine blocks remote content in pages loaded from local files by
default, so an iframe in a local HTML file showed an error page instead
of the embedded site. Allow it, as the Plasma 5 widget and browsers do.

BUG: 484617

patches.diff:
From 36721757db586b4fc31d63a774ac21d242a7c4c0 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: =?UTF-8?q?Niccol=C3=B2=20Venerandi?= <niccolo@venerandi.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 16:36:41 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] applets/webbrowser: let local pages show remote content

Qt WebEngine blocks remote content in pages loaded from local files by
default, so an iframe in a local HTML file showed an error page instead
of the embedded site. Allow it, as the Plasma 5 widget and browsers do.

BUG: 484617
---
 applets/webbrowser/qml/main.qml | 1 +
 1 file changed, 1 insertion(+)

diff --git a/applets/webbrowser/qml/main.qml b/applets/webbrowser/qml/main.qml
index 38c005eb0..2f9a52605 100644
--- a/applets/webbrowser/qml/main.qml
+++ b/applets/webbrowser/qml/main.qml
@@ -257,6 +257,7 @@ PlasmoidItem {
                 anchors.fill: parent
                 settings.javascriptCanAccessClipboard: true
                 settings.javascriptCanPaste: true
+                settings.localContentCanAccessRemoteUrls: true
                 onUrlChanged: Plasmoid.configuration.url = url;
                 Component.onCompleted: url = Plasmoid.configuration.useDefaultUrl ? Plasmoid.configuration.defaultUrl : Plasmoid.configuration.url;
                 settings.fullScreenSupportEnabled: true
--

media.caption: A local HTML file with an iframe to an http page: the iframe shows the error page
Same file with the fix: the iframe shows the remote page

review.text: Setting settings.localContentCanAccessRemoteUrls: true does allow remote iframes inside file:// pages, but in QtWebEngine this maps to Blink's allow_universal_access_from_file_urls, which disables the Same-Origin Policy for local HTML files against the widget's shared persistent WebEngineProfile (while localContentCanAccessFileUrls remains true). That is significantly more permissive than standard browsers, and both the commit message ('as the Plasma 5 widget and browsers do') and explanation ('The Plasma 5 (QtWebKit) widget allowed it') are factually inaccurate since Plasma 5's webbrowser widget used QtWebEngine and browsers do not grant universal cross-origin access to file:// pages.
changes: Re-evaluate enabling settings.localContentCanAccessRemoteUrls: true unconditionally given that it enables Chromium's allow_universal_access_from_file_urls (bypassing Same-Origin Policy for file:// pages against a persistent WebEngineProfile); consider gating it behind an opt-in widget setting or obtaining explicit Plasma/security review and documenting the trade-off.

Correct the inaccurate claims in the commit message and entry explanation: Plasma 5's webbrowser widget used QtWebEngine (not QtWebKit), and standard browsers allow remote iframes in file:// pages without granting universal cross-origin access.

reviews.text: This is the correct root cause and the minimal fix: Qt WebEngine defaults localContentCanAccessRemoteUrls to false, so file:// pages can't load remote iframes. Setting it on the widget's WebEngineView restores the Plasma 5 behaviour that the reporter and Nate's minimal file depend on. The before/after screenshots show the sad-page iframe replaced by the remote content, and a normal https page still loads. One thing to state in the MR: with localContentCanAccessFileUrls still at its default (true), a local page loaded in the widget can now both read other local files and reach the network. That is acceptable for a widget showing the user's own pages, and it matches Plasma 5, but the commit's 'as browsers do' only holds for the iframe part.
